name: OU Jobs (Partner)
desc:
Admissions and Recruitment Assistant | $15.00/hr | Data Entry and Document Review, Minimal Phone-SEASONAL Aug-March
Company: University of Oklahoma (PEAK Temporary Staffing)
Industry: Higher Education | Admissions Support
What Your Day Will Look Like:
 This is a seasonal, temporary position with OU's Office of Admissions and Recruitment, running mid-August through March. You're part of the behind the scenes team that keeps the college application review process moving, prepping application files, auditing the holistic review process, and helping make sure applications get processed accurately and efficiently during the busy admissions cycle.
Day to day, this looks like reading applications, performing curricular review, and generally supporting the file preparation pipeline so admissions counselors and reviewers have clean, organized applications to work from. This is detail heavy, document focused work rather than a phone-heavy role, so if you're the type who likes quietly working through a stack of files with accuracy and care, this fits well.
Because this is a PEAK (temporary staffing) position through OU, it's genuinely time-limited by design, running through one admissions cycle rather than being an ongoing role, though the flexible 20 to 30 hour a week schedule could work well alongside other commitments.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: High school diploma or GED.
 Required Experience: 12 months of office, clerical, or administrative support experience.
 Preferred Experience: Not separately broken out.
 Required Skills:
Working knowledge of general office procedures
Customer service skills
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word)
Excellent interpersonal skills
Ability to work independently and as part of a team
Strong attention to detail for data accuracy
Ability to multitask and stay organized
Ability to work under stress
Strong verbal and written communication
Best Fit
This role is ideal for:
Someone with prior clerical or administrative experience who prefers detail-focused document work over phone-heavy roles
Participants who want flexible part-time hours during a specific seasonal window
Anyone interested in getting a foot in the door with a large, stable state institution
People who work well independently with minimal day to day oversight
Not a Good Fit for:
Participants who need permanent, year-round employment, since this is explicitly a temporary seasonal role
Anyone who needs benefits eligibility, since this position is not benefits eligible
Someone who prefers phone-based customer interaction over document review and data entry
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
 Administrative support, clerical, data entry, document review, Microsoft Office, application processing, detail oriented, office procedures, organization, higher education administratio
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:

Applicants complete a Personal Profile through the OU PEAK Jobs Application system, then apply to the specific PEAK position through jobs.ou.edu. Background check is confirmed as a requirement for hire.
Likely interview questions for this role:
Tell me about your experience with detail-oriented administrative or clerical work.
How do you stay accurate and organized when reviewing a high volume of documents or files?
Describe a time you worked independently to complete a task with a deadline.
How do you handle stress during a busy processing period?
other:
Good context for participants: Oklahoma has a statewide ban-the-box executive order that applies to state agencies, and OU is a state institution, so this application will not ask about criminal history upfront. A background check does happen later in the hiring process, but a felony conviction does not automatically disqualify someone, the university is required to individually assess whether the conviction actually relates to the specific job duties before making a decision. This is a genuinely more favorable process than a lot of private employers in this database.
This is a temporary, seasonal role tied to the admissions cycle (mid-August through March), not year-round work, and it is not benefits eligible. Set that expectation clearly with participants.
Pay is modest at $15/hr, but the flexible 20-30 hour schedule could work well for someone balancing other responsibilities or a second job.
Career Pathway: PEAK Admissions and Recruitment Assistant (Temporary) → Admissions Coordinator → Assistant Director of Admissions → Associate Director of Admissions → Director of Admissions
